lye.e: From Middle English leye, lye, from Old English lēah, lēag (“lye”), from Proto-West Germanic *laugu, from Proto-Germanic *laugō, from Proto-Indo-European *lewh₃- (“to wash”). Russian м́ыло (ḿylo) (a nomen instrumenti of мыть (mytʹ)).
lye.g: An alkaline liquid made by leaching ashes (usually wood ashes).

lye.e: Variant of lie (“to rest horizontally”) now used in a specialised sense; compare sett.

lying.e: lie (“to rest in a horizontal position”) + -ing.
lying.g: The act of one who lies, or keeps low to the ground.

lyre.e: From Middle English lire (13th c.), from Old French lire, from Latin lyra, from Ancient Greek λύρᾱ (lúrā, “lyre, a stringed instrument with a sounding-board formed of the shell of a tortoise”).
lyre.g: An ancient stringed musical instrument (a yoke lute chordophone) of Greek origin, consisting of two arms extending from a body to a crossbar
